classifications.rationale: The President presently designates the Commissioned Corps as a military service and branch of the armed forces for a defined period, immediately changing its legal status from the order's date through June 1, 1952.
classifications.evidence: I hereby declare the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service to be a military service and a branch of the land and naval forces of the Untied States from the date of this order to and including June 1, 1952.

classifications.rationale: The provision itself makes the Commissioned Corps subject to the Uniform Code of Military Justice during the designated period and presently adapts that code to its officers, creating immediate legal duties and exposure.
classifications.evidence: The Uniform Code of Military Justice is hereby adapted to apply to officers of the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service

classifications.rationale: The provision itself makes Corps members who violate the Uniform Code subject to trial and punishment, while also presently assigning related statutory authorities to named officials; the legal consequence arises under this provision rather than through a mandated later agency rule.
classifications.evidence: Any member of the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service who violates any provision of the Uniform Code of Military Justice shall be subject to trial and punishment as prescribed therein.

classifications.rationale: The provision presently subjects detailed officers and Public Health Service courts-martial to specified legal regimes, preserves enforcement of existing liabilities, and limits punishment; these consequences operate directly rather than awaiting a prescribed agency outcome.
classifications.evidence: Commissioned officers of the Public Health Service now or hereafter detailed for duty with the armed forces shall be subject to the laws applicable to the service to which they are detailed as prescribed by law.
